title: Save a huge $1,020 on a 240Hz OLED gaming laptop from Lenovo with an RTX 5070 Ti, now just $1,999
summary: Grab a 16-inch OLED gaming laptop with an RTX 5070 Ti from Lenovo for just $1,999.99 right now.
content: An OLED gaming laptop, fitted with an RTX 5070 Ti, and all for less than $2,000? That's a deal you don't want to ignore. Lenovo has slashed $1,020 off this Lenovo Legion 5i OLED gaming laptop, dropping the price down to just $1,999.99 for Black Friday . While the RTX 5070 Ti is a powerhouse, it's the 16-inch OLED display with its 240Hz refresh rate that makes a real difference here. ● Check out this OLED gaming laptop at Lenovo Choosing OLED over a basic LCD means you're getting a display that'll give you perfect blacks and almost infinite contrast, while that 240Hz refresh rate is ultra-fast and ideal for smooth, blur-free motion in games. The top resolution here is 2,560 x 1,600, and with the RTX 5070 Ti at your disposal, you won't struggle to hit high frame rates with ultra graphics presets switched on at 1600p. You've also got the option to hook it up to an external display over HDMI if you want to go bigger. Legion 5i Gaming Laptop (Core Ultra 7 251HX, RTX 5070 Ti): was $3019.99 now $1999.99 This Lenovo Legion 5i gaming laptop sports an Intel Core Ultra 7 251 HX, RTX 5070 Ti GPU, 16GB of DDR5 and 1TB of NVMe storage. This is an OLED gaming laptop with a 1600p top resolution and a 240Hz refresh rate. View Deal The gaming credentials, though, are confirmed by the RTX 5070 Ti. Yes, it's the mobile version, so it isn't a like-for-like with its desktop equivalent, and instead ships with a set of 5,888 CUDA cores and 12GB GDDR7 VRAM. At 1600p, though, that won't be much of a problem. DLSS support, meanwhile, means you've got breathing room, with multi-frame generation able to cut some of the slack with AI-generated frames to give you an uplift in the most power-intensive games. Coupled with the GPU is the Intel Core Ultra 7 251HX as your processor. It has 18 cores, comprised of six performance cores and 12 efficient cores, with a max boost clock on the p-cores of up to 5.1 GHz. Again, a more than formidable option for the kind of gaming or productivity work you'd be expected to do on a laptop like this. Elsewhere, you're getting a 1TB SSD offering Gen 4 speeds, so enough space for a couple of big game installations there. A small compromise is on RAM, with only 16GB of DDR5 included here. While 32GB would be better, the price is good, and you've got the option to upgrade later down the line. You're also getting multiple USB-C ports, Gigabit Ethernet, a 3.5mm headphone jack, and the aforementioned HDMI. It also includes Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 5.4 connectivity. The $1,999 sale price for this Lenovo Legion 5i Gen 10 OLED gaming laptop is a seriously good one in the current market. You'll struggle to find similar specs for less than $2,000 elsewhere, so expect this deal to sell out quickly, and make your own moves to buy it accordingly. title: Ukrainian 11th-grader builds AI-powered, GPS-free drone autopilot to beat frontline jamming
summary: Yaroslav Sheiko's innovation allows drones to fly accurately even if they don't have a GPS signal or encounter GPS jamming.
content: An 11th-grade student has received “The Future of Ukraine” from President Volodymyr Zelenskyy for multiple technical achievements. According to Poltava Wave , Yaroslav Sheiko, a student from Poltava, located about 190 miles to the west of Kyiv, built an AI-powered drone autopilot system, allowing uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) to reach their destination without relying on GPS signals, and an optical-electronic stabilization system. This award is just the latest among Sheiko’s achievements. The 11th-grader has already received two presidential scholarships for his academic performance and contributions to science, as well as getting the top award twice in nationwide competitions held by Ukraine’s Junior Academy of Sciences. He has also competed internationally, receiving a gold medal in the INOVA 2025 International Inventions Show and a silver medal in the 2025 Hackathon. Even though Ukraine relies on military assistance from its allies, it’s also working on homegrown technologies to improve its drone capabilities. Some of these breakthroughs include equipping its grounded fleet of U.S.-made Puma reconnaissance drones with domestic anti-jamming systems and using a network of “flying modems” to increase the range of its attack drones without having to use unreliable Starlink connections . It was the first to use a heavy-lift UAV to evacuate a wounded soldier from a minefield and conduct a 12-hour, 1,500-mile strategic drone strike on Russian targets. The country is also working on anti-drone systems, like using old Android phones as an acoustic sensor network as an early warning system to spot drones and shooting down Russian jet drones using a cheap, high-powered laser air defense system. The widespread use of drones in Ukraine also meant that other countries have started developing their own drone and anti-drone technologies and forces. China has revealed a 200-strong AI drone swarm controlled by a single soldier using an “intelligent algorithm,” while Japan is working on an ultra-cheap cardboard drone swarm that only costs $2,000 per unit. The UK is also deploying the DragonFire anti-drone laser on Royal Navy destroyers by 2027.
